item.title: SUNY reports rebounding enrollment and stabilized budgets
item.description: SUNY has seen three years of student growth and a stabilized budget, and is on track to close a $1 billion budget gap within a decade, although the state's main student financial aid program is losing purchasing power.

item.title: How much do immigrants pay in taxes?
item.description: Foreign-born New Yorkers contribute significantly to the state's economy, paying billions in taxes and fees, and the New York for All Act seeks to protect these contributions by preventing state and local agencies from cooperating with federal immigration enforcement.

item.title: MVHS to move several offices
item.description: UTICA, NY (WUTR/WFXV/WPNY) -- The Mohawk Valley Health System has announced that several offices will be moving to a centralized location on State Street. item.title: Lawmakers propose liquor at grocery stores and cannabis beverages at liquor stores
item.description: Democratic lawmakers in New York have introduced bills that would allow supermarkets and local bodegas to sell hard alcohol and wine, and liquor stores to sell low-potency weed beverages, with the goal of modernizing the state's alcohol laws and boosting vineyards, agricultural businesses, and the craft spirits industry.

item.title: Ben Rizzo, Utica pro football player, dies at 86
item.description: A Greater Utica Sports Hall of Fame inductee and Utica Notre Dame coaching legend has passed away at the age of 86.

item.title: Advocates rally to end ICE detention contracts and 287(g) agreements
item.description: New Yorkers rallied at the Capitol to push for two bills that would cut ties between the state and federal immigration enforcement, including ending 287(g) agreements and contracts that pay local facilities to hold people arrested by ICE.

item.title: State Republicans and Democrats Launch Bills for Affordability
item.description: Many New Yorkers around the state have felt steep prices in their wallet, especially when healthcare and utility bills were due. On February 24, two different announcements were made in the state capitol as Democrat and Republican lawmakers pushed aid to all of New York.
